message: Physics-simulated melee in online PvP is hard to network: ragdoll and contact results diverge between clients.
probe: Would you accept server-authoritative physics with input delay, or keep PvP local or co-op only?

message: An MMO needs servers, live ops and content volume far beyond a solo or very small team.
probe: Could this be a small-session online game or a single-player game with MMO flavor instead?

message: Permadeath on a long authored campaign makes players replay hours of fixed content after one mistake.
probe: Should death end a run, or should a long campaign use a softer penalty?

message: Deep authored branching on a procedural world is expensive: every branch must work in spaces you did not hand-place.
probe: Is the story allowed to be emergent, or should story locations be handcrafted inside the procedural world?

message: Free-to-play revenue depends on ongoing content and offers; a finished product gives players little reason to keep spending.
probe: Is this premium after all, or are you planning seasons and a content pipeline?

message: Long sessions with deep simulation fit poorly on mobile, where play happens in short bursts on small screens.
probe: Should sessions be chunked into short goals that save and resume instantly?

message: Matches of 100 or more players demand netcode, servers, anti-cheat and a large player base to fill lobbies.
probe: Would a smaller lobby, or bots that fill matches, protect launch?

message: Strict survival needs fight a cozy, relaxed tone: starvation timers create anxiety.
probe: Should food give bonuses instead of threatening death?

message: Fast artificial locomotion in VR causes motion sickness for many players.
probe: Will you offer teleport, snap turning and vignette comfort options, or design around room-scale movement?

message: An open world cannot be built and filled in a game jam.
probe: Can the jam version be one small, dense area that proves the core loop?

message: Systemic enemies that remember and rank against the player resemble the Nemesis system, which Warner Bros. patented (US 10,926,179, granted 23 February 2021).
probe: How will your adaptive enemies differ from the patented Nemesis design? Consider legal review before cloning it literally.

message: A player-driven market needs online players to trade with.
probe: Is this an online game, or should the market be simulated by NPC traders?

message: A vast handcrafted world is a huge content load for one developer.
probe: Could procedural generation or a smaller, denser world carry the same fantasy?

message: A persistent online world cannot be built, secured and operated in a few months.
probe: Could launch use session-based matches and add persistence later?

message: A punishing single difficulty with an all-ages audience will lose younger or casual players.
probe: Would an assist mode keep the intended challenge while widening the audience?

message: Selling power in a competitive game reads as pay-to-win and erodes trust.
probe: Can monetization stay cosmetic in competitive modes?

message: Ironman saves on mobile need instant suspend and resume, because the OS kills apps at any time.
probe: Will the game autosave on every state change?

message: Simulated ballistics plus heavy aim assist blurs the skill expression that ballistics is meant to create.
probe: Is the goal accessibility or marksmanship?

message: Full destruction in online play means syncing large amounts of world state.
probe: Can destruction be limited to authored pieces or deterministic chunks?

message: Soft-body vehicle damage is CPU heavy; many networked vehicles at once will strain clients and servers.
probe: Will soft-body run only locally, with simplified damage shared online?

message: Emergent stories need room for systems to collide; a linear world limits that space.
probe: Would a hub or sandbox structure give systems room to create stories?

message: Wordless teaching on mobile risks early churn; players there leave quickly when lost.
probe: Will you add an optional hint system?

message: Losing loot on death is a punishing hook that clashes with an accessible target audience.
probe: Should insurance, safe slots or a practice mode soften the loss?

message: A real-time clock rewards daily check-ins more than long sittings.
probe: Is the intended habit daily visits or long sessions?

message: Visible damage numbers with otherwise hidden systems sends mixed signals about how much math players should engage with.
probe: Which systems should players be able to calculate?

message: Deep branching dialogue multiplies writing and voice costs quickly for a small team.
probe: Will the protagonist be unvoiced, or will branches reconverge often?

message: A rhythm game with gameplay independent of the music contradicts its genre promise.
probe: Should core actions land on the beat?

message: A power fantasy drains horror of tension; fear needs vulnerability.
probe: Where in the game does the player feel powerless?

message: Idle games are built on low attention; intense pace works against offline progress.
probe: Is the active layer optional, or is this really an incremental action game?

message: Phone-as-controller party games usually rely on a shared screen; online play needs streaming or voice.
probe: Is the target a shared room or remote play over streaming?

message: Selling gear that can be lost on death invites accusations of predatory design.
probe: Should purchasable items be cosmetic or protected from loss?

message: This scope does not fit the timeline.
probe: Which single pillar must ship, and what can be cut to a later update?

message: Visceral gore will not get an all-ages rating.
probe: Is the audience all ages, or should violence be stylized?

message: Turn-based time with execution-first cadence is unusual: turns remove the time pressure that tests execution.
probe: Is there a timing element inside turns, like timed hits?

message: Procedural levels and precision platforming conflict: tight jumps need hand-tuned geometry.
probe: Will generation assemble handmade rooms rather than raw terrain?
